The Next Set Of AI Winners

Udith Sikand, Rohan Daswani

Gavekal Research | 14 Aug 2026

As the S&P 500 edged up to yet another record close on Thursday, it was clear US investors had mostly shrugged off the jitters of recent weeks. Underpinning this latest gain is a bet—whether explicit or implicit—that capital expenditure on artificial intelligence will deliver the hoped-for productivity gains on a scale sufficient to turbocharge economic growth. Meanwhile, the AI Jeremiahs continue to warn the current pace of capex is unsustainable.Either way, the AI boom is leading to big macroeconomic effects. In the US, the contribution to GDP growth from AI capex now regularly exceeds the contribution from consumption (see Is AI Capex Driving US Growth?). In the first quarter of 2026, both South Korea and Taiwan recorded nominal GDP growth of more than 17% YoY, driven by surging demand for AI-related semiconductors. And more than half the increase in China’s exports over recent months has been driven by shipments of AI-related goods (see China’s Supporting Role In The AI Boom).
